```typescript
type AcademyContentBlock =
  | { type: 'heading'; content: string; level?: 2 | 3 }
  | { type: 'paragraph'; content: string }
  | { type: 'code'; content: string; language?: string }
  | { type: 'callout'; content: string; variant?: 'info' | 'warning' | 'tip' }
  | { type: 'table'; headers: string[]; rows: string[][] }
  | { type: 'link-card'; title: string; url: string; description: string; source?: string }
  | { type: 'tool-card'; name: string; category: string; description: string; url?: string; features?: string[] }
```

---

**Section 1: AI-Powered IDEs & Editors**

Cover these categories with tool-cards and comparison tables:

**GUI IDEs:**
- **Cursor** — AI-first IDE built on VS Code. Features: tab completion, chat, composer, multi-file edits. url: https://cursor.sh
- **Google Antigravity** — Google's AI IDE, deep Gemini integration. Features: cloud workspaces, Gemini models built-in. url: https://idx.google.com
- **Kiro** — AWS-backed AI IDE with spec-driven development. Features: spec files, hooks, steering docs. url: https://kiro.dev
- **Windsurf** — Codeium's AI IDE with Cascade. Features: Cascade multi-step agent, memory across sessions. url: https://codeium.com/windsurf
- **GitHub Copilot** — The original AI coding assistant. Features: inline completions, chat, Copilot Workspace. url: https://github.com/features/copilot

**Terminal Agents:**
- **Claude Code** — Anthropic's CLI agent. Features: CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP, agent teams. url: https://claude.ai/claude-code
- **Codex CLI** — OpenAI's terminal agent. Features: sandboxed execution, multi-file edits. url: https://github.com/openai/codex
- **Gemini CLI** — Google's terminal agent. Features: Gemini models, Google integrations. url: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli
- **Aider** — Open-source AI pair programmer. Features: git integration, multi-model support, repo-map. url: https://aider.chat

**VS Code Extensions:**
- **Cline** — Autonomous coding agent. Features: multi-step execution, tool use, MCP support. url: https://github.com/cline/cline
- **Roo Code** — Fork of Cline with extra features. Features: custom modes, MCP marketplace. url: https://github.com/RooVetGit/Roo-Code
- **Continue** — Open-source AI assistant. Features: autocomplete, chat, multi-model. url: https://continue.dev

Include:
1. Opening heading and paragraph introducing the landscape
2. A comparison table: headers ["Tool", "Type", "Key Strength", "Best For"], 5-8 rows
3. Tool cards for each tool organized by category headings
4. A callout (variant: 'tip') about choosing the right tool

---

**Section 2: AI Code Review & Quality**

Cover these tools:
- **CodeRabbit** — AI code reviewer that integrates with GitHub/GitLab PRs. Features: auto-review, security scanning, one-click fixes. url: https://coderabbit.ai
- **Greptile** — AI that understands your entire codebase. Features: codebase-aware reviews, Slack integration. url: https://greptile.com
- **Qodo** (formerly CodiumAI) — AI test generation and review. Features: test generation, PR review, code integrity. url: https://qodo.ai
- **Ellipsis** — Automated code review bot. Features: auto-fix PRs, custom rules, security checks. url: https://ellipsis.dev
- **Cursor BugBot** — Bug detection within Cursor IDE. Features: automated bug finding, inline fixes.

Include:
1. Opening heading and paragraph on why AI code review matters
2. A callout (variant: 'info') with stat: "Teams using AI code review report 30-50% fewer bugs in production"
3. Tool cards for each tool
4. A table comparing features: headers ["Tool", "Reviews PRs", "Security Scan", "Test Gen", "Self-Service"]
5. Best practices paragraph

**Guidelines:**
- Do NOT use \! in any strings (causes TS1127)
- Make content informative and practical
- Use tool-card type for individual tools, table type for comparisons
- Each section should have 15-25 content blocks
